item.title: Bard College President Botstein’s continued leadership is no longer tenable
item.description: When someone has held power for nearly half a century, it can become easy to confuse longevity with legitimacy, or position with immunity. But tenure is not a substitute for trust.

item.title: Nelsons to step down as BSO music director after 2027 Tanglewood season
item.description: Board cites differences over the orchestra’s future direction.

item.title: Stockbridge Select Board discusses latest iteration of fiscal 2027 operational and capital budgets, includes proposed road improvements
item.description: Updates to the budget include a Climate Leaders Program free cash expense and Chapter 90 road improvements.

item.title: THEN & NOW: The original location of Catherine’s Chocolates, now home to Farnsworth Fine Cannabis Company
item.description: The 126 Main Street site was renovated and enlarged, serving as home to numerous businesses over the years, including Farnsworth Fine Cannabis Company.

item.title: I WITNESS: Of surgical lethality and window dressings
item.description: There is nothing "surgical" about the operation, nothing "surgical" about chaos, destruction, and death. In medical terms, if the patient doesn't survive the surgery, it was not quite surgical enough.

item.title: Massachusetts Board of Library Commissioners approves design of new Otis Library building
item.description: "We are where people come to meet new people, where new communities form—we have some people who come every week, maybe more than once a week. If you have a question about Otis, this is where you come. That is what we’re here for…I feel like we are the heart and soul of the town,” said Otis Library Director Stephanie Skinner.

item.title: Martha Louise Hawkins (née Moore), 87, of Great Barrington
item.description: Martha’s legacy is one of connection, warmth, and shared laughter. Her memory will continue to inspire all who were fortunate enough to know her.

item.title: Berkshire performing arts organizations receive state grants
item.description: "This funding ensures [these performing arts centers] can continue to attract exceptional touring performances, expand access to high-quality arts experiences, and strengthen local economies across Massachusetts,” said Mass Cultural Council Acting Executive Director David T. Slatery.

item.title: PREVIEW: Close Encounters with Music presents ‘Mostly Amadeus—Meet the Mozarts!’ March 15 at the Mahaiwe
item.description: From Leopold Mozart’s teaching and promotion of his son’s early career to the later compositions of Franz Xaver Mozart, the program traces the musical lineage surrounding one of history’s most celebrated composers.

item.title: THE OTHER SIDE: War once more
item.description: It is, of course, the innocent who suffer most in these wars of choice.
